title: Operational Playbook: Observability-driven Refresh & Promotion for Verified Runtime Profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a concrete operational playbook to automatically detect when a Redwood-verified performance profile (latency/throughput/cost) is stale, trigger an automated rebenchmark, and promote validated revisions via a safe canary + audit trail. Current onboarding creates verified profiles manually and publishes them as immutable artifacts; over time model binaries, kernels, and serving infra change and profiles drift. This ticket defines the observability signals, governance gates, promotion mechanics, and rollback strategy so we can maintain trustworthy published profiles without manual re-certification for every minor infra change.
acceptance_criteria: Define a minimal set of drift signals (90th p99 latency delta, throughput degradation %, token-cost variance) and document thresholds for auto-refresh
Implement an automated job that detects candidate profiles for refresh and queues them for re-benchmarking with the same test harness used by verification
Support staged promotion: staging profile artifact -> running canary traffic (internal) -> opt-in customers -> full promotion with signed audit record
Published profile artifacts are stored in git-backed registry with semantic version and signed metadata (who/when/commit/hash)
Ability to pin customers to specific profile versions and a migration UX for mass-pinned accounts with clear risk messages
Monitoring dashboards and alerts exist for refresh failures, promotion anomalies, and rollback operations
implementation_notes: Drift signals: compare nightly aggregated snapshots per model-variant/hardware pair. Primary signals: median latency shift > 10% AND p99 shift > 5ms, throughput drop > 8%, cost-per-token change > 5% after normalizing batch sizes.

Re-benchmark harness should reuse model weights and input corpora from onboarding (seeded prompts + traffic-sampled sequences). Ensure determinism in kernel selection flags to isolate infra vs model changes.

Profiles remain immutable once promoted; new revisions use semantic increment (v1 -> v1.1) and link to parent. Promotion writes a signed release entry (GPG/HSM) with metadata: infra-version, kernel-hash, benchmark-commit, dataset-hash.
Canary flow: run new profile on dedicated canary pool for 48 hours with synthetic and low-volume internal traffic. Must meet acceptance thresholds before broader opt-in.
Rollback: store previous profile pointer and an automated revert job that reassigns traffic and reopens a rollback incident with pre-populated runbook steps.
We will expose a /profiles API extension: GET /profiles/{model}/{variant}?version= to fetch metadata and a header indicating verified=true and signature.
Security: store signature keys in KMS. Audit logs for promotions must be retained for 1 year (legal requirement for enterprise customers).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): Build detection job and dashboard. Wire drift signals into a muted alert channel for SRE to validate noise levels.
Phase 2 (week 3): Implement automated re-benchmark pipeline that can be triggered by detection job. Run dry-runs against 10 historical profiles to validate false positive rates.
Phase 3 (week 4): Add canary promotion plumbing and signed artifact storage. Enable internal opt-in list for product/SE teams.
Phase 4 (week 5-6): Expose opt-in to selected customers and perform two staged promotions. Collect telemetry and launch customer communications template.
Phase 5 (week 7): Open full promotion path and enable automatic promotions for low-risk model-variant pairs. Monitor for 30 days before declaring GA.
Rollback window: initial automatic promotions will include a 72-hour manual hold before finalizing audit records to permit fast human rollback if needed.
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboard: profile-refresh-candidates (count), avg time-to-refresh, acceptance-pass-rate, canary-failure-rate
Alerts: high false-positive rate (>15% of detection jobs flagged but fail re-benchmark), canary failure (any acceptance threshold failure), promotion error (signature or registry write failures)
SLOs: re-benchmark job success >= 98% over 30-day window; promotion pipeline latency < 6 hours end-to-end for automated low-risk promotions
migration_and_pin_strategy: Customers pinned to exact profile versions continue serving unchanged; provide a migration API that lists recommended target profiles and estimated delta in latency/cost for each target
Mass migration tool: allow customer success to run opt-in campaigns per-account with staged traffic increases (10% -> 50% -> 100%), and automated rollback hooks if metrics deviate
Communications: generate templated release notes for promoted profile revisions including observed deltas, test harness link, and rollback instructions
Policy: any profile revision with cost increase >10% or p99 latency regression >10ms requires manual PM + SRE approval before promotion
